sketches.title: The Playground Crown
sketches.premise: Two playground troublemakers compete to claim the best spot, tool, or advantage. Each turn, name one playground thing and use it to defeat what is currently in charge.
sketches.criterion: A move overcomes the standing thing by plainly taking, trapping, blocking, wearing out, or making useless what it is, while merely hiding, lasting longer, or choosing a bigger version loses.
sketches.move_shape: Say what you are and how you take over: "I am the sandbox, burying your marble run under a landslide of sand." The host sighs that the marble run has finally met a problem it cannot roll away from.
sketches.first_card: I am the slide, sending the empty swing out of the way.

sketches.title: Recess Rescue Chain
sketches.premise: A playground problem appears, and players answer with a playground helper that fixes it. Every move must solve the thing before it, so the chain keeps getting more ridiculous while still making sense.
sketches.criterion: A move overcomes the standing problem by directly fixing, stopping, freeing, or replacing it; dodging it, merely enduring it, or using a bigger copy of the same problem does not count.
sketches.move_shape: Say what you are and what you repair: "I am a broom, sweeping the puddle off the hopscotch squares." The host notes that the puddle has been promoted to a weather system and still lost to household equipment.
sketches.first_card: I am a puddle, flooding the chalk drawing.

sketches.title: Tag, You’re It Until You’re Not
sketches.premise: One playground thing is chasing another through words. On your turn, become something that can catch or stop the current chaser, then explain the capture in one sentence.
sketches.criterion: A move overcomes the standing thing by physically catching, pinning, enclosing, or stopping it; running away, being too small to notice, or becoming a larger version of it is a loss.
sketches.move_shape: Say what you are and how you catch it: "I am a net, wrapping the ball before it reaches the fence." The host calls this a bold strategy: letting string do the running.
sketches.first_card: I am a runaway ball, bouncing toward the gate.

sketches.title: The Sandbox Court
sketches.premise: Every turn puts a new playground object on trial for causing a mess. The next player names a playground object that can plainly control or clean up the accused thing.
sketches.criterion: A move overcomes the standing object by containing, cleaning, covering, breaking, or putting it where it belongs; simply avoiding it, surviving it, or offering a bigger relative is not a verdict.
sketches.move_shape: Say what you are and deliver the ruling: "I am a bucket, containing the sandstorm you started." The host declares the sand guilty of being everywhere and the bucket guilty of having a handle.
sketches.first_card: I am spilled sand, covering the whole sandbox.

sketches.title: Recess Forecast
sketches.premise: The playground is having a very strange day, and each turn changes the conditions. Name a playground thing that directly defeats the current weather, mess, or hazard, not one that merely waits it out.
sketches.criterion: A move overcomes what stands by blocking, drying, clearing, cooling, or otherwise canceling its effect; hiding from it, surviving it, or making it larger is not overcoming.
sketches.move_shape: Say what you are and change the forecast: "I am a roof, keeping the rain off the climbing frame." The host admits the rain has been outsmarted by architecture, which is humiliating but legal.
sketches.first_card: I am rain, soaking the playground.

sketches.title: The Playground Machine
sketches.premise: The playground becomes a friendly chain of machines, tools, and structures, each one built to defeat the thing before it. Keep the answer to something a child could find, carry, climb, or imagine at recess.
sketches.criterion: A move overcomes the standing thing by using a clear function to lift, cut, lock, sweep, crush, hold, or redirect it; merely escaping, resisting, or presenting a bigger member of its family loses.
sketches.move_shape: Say what you are and use your function: "I am a lever, lifting the heavy seesaw seat." The host observes that the seesaw has been defeated by a stick with confidence and basic physics.
sketches.first_card: I am a stuck gate, refusing to open.
